headline: Nifty at nine-month high meets a global AI sell-off; gap-down open signalled

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Friday, the twentieth of November, and here is your Market Brief.

Three things matter this morning. First, Indian shares closed Thursday at nine-month highs, with the Nifty above 25,500 for the first time since February. But a fresh global sell-off overnight means today could open sharply lower. GIFT Nifty is down more than 200 points.

Second, that sell-off came on the very day Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, made the largest stock market debut in history on the Nasdaq. The shares jumped, but the excitement did not spread. Wall Street fell about 2 percent, and Asia is falling harder this morning.

And third, at home, inflation and the harvest are the worries. Retail inflation hit a two-year high of 6.1 percent in October, and rabi sowing is down 11 percent after a dry autumn.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Thursday was a strong day. The Sensex rose about 990 points, or 1.2 percent, to reclaim 83,000. The Nifty gained 1.1 percent and closed above 25,500 for the first time in nine months. The Bank Nifty hit a record above 63,000.

Autos, banks and consumer durables led the way, helped by easing crude prices, foreign buying and a firmer rupee.

On the other side, information technology fell for a third straight day. The Nifty IT index has lost 4.5 percent in three sessions and is down about 6.5 percent this month. Smaller companies tied to the global AI and data-centre trade have been hit hard. Sterlite Technologies and HFCL are down as much as 29 percent in a month. Fintech shares like Paytm, Pine Labs and MobiKwik fell up to 9 percent on reports that a planned fee on some high-value UPI payments may be delayed.

The money flows tell the story of this rally. Foreign portfolio investors were net buyers again on Thursday, while domestic institutions sold. In the first half of November, foreign investors poured in a record 84,000 crore rupees, more than half of it into financial stocks. For November so far, the Nifty is up nearly 11 percent and the Sensex about 11.5 percent. Both are heading for a fourth straight weekly gain. The rupee firmed for a fourth session to 93.30 to the dollar.

The views are turning warmer too. Goldman Sachs upgraded India to overweight with a Nifty target of 28,500 for December 2027. A global fund manager survey shows managers overweight on India for the first time since January, and Jefferies' Chris Wood has raised his India exposure. Some analysts caution, though, that rising bond yields are making shares look expensive.

Now the levels. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see support near 25,400, then 25,300 to 25,200, and a firmer floor at 25,100 to 25,000. On the upside, a sustained move above 25,500 could open the way to 25,650 and 25,800.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to the primary market. The Mahanadi Coalfields issue drew 38 percent subscription on its first day.

Three big filings came in. Sagar Defence Engineering, which makes unmanned maritime systems, filed updated papers for a 3,412 crore rupee issue. That's 1,200 crore of fresh shares and about 2,212 crore sold by promoters. NLC India Renewables, the green energy arm of the state-run lignite miner, plans to raise 3,300 crore rupees through fresh shares, with 2,475 crore going to repay debt. And Eldorado Agritech has halved its issue to 504 crore rupees.

Razorpay, backed by Tiger Global, is preparing to file next week and could launch as early as February.

A number for perspective. Companies that listed this year have added about 32 lakh crore rupees to the BSE's market value. Jio Platforms alone accounts for 41 percent of that.

In deals, Fairfax raised its stake in IIFL Capital Services to 52.63 percent, buying shares worth 1,540 crore rupees. And Sebi says its roadmap focuses on faster IPO and rights issue timelines, plus a market-making framework to make corporate bonds easier to trade.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
A quiet day for results, but two numbers stand out. Public sector banks posted their highest-ever net profit for the first half of this financial year, 1.09 lakh crore rupees. Their capital adequacy ratio improved to 16.89 percent at the end of September.

And Tata Technologies jumped over 9 percent after setting a revenue target of 1.1 to 1.3 billion dollars by the 2030 financial year, roughly double last year's level.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy, and inflation first. Retail inflation reached a two-year high of 6.1 percent in October. Elara Securities economist Garima Kapoor expects it to stay above 6 percent through March, and she sees two quarter-point rate hikes from the Reserve Bank. Rahul Bhutoria of Valtrust also expects another hike in December.

Growth is cooling a little. Rating agency ICRA expects September quarter growth at 7.5 percent, a five-quarter low, down from 7.8 percent. And the farm picture is worrying. Rabi sowing is down 11.3 percent. Wheat acreage has fallen 15 percent and pulses 14 percent, with post-monsoon rain 34 percent below normal.

On trade, Piyush Goyal is aiming for one trillion dollars of exports this year. October was a record month at about 90 billion dollars. Even so, India needs around 430 billion dollars more between November and March to get there.

One trade dispute to note. Revenue intelligence officials have applied an effective 162.5 percent duty on bulk Scotch imports, higher than before the trade deal with Britain. The Centre is working to resolve it.

The government also raised the windfall tax on diesel exports to 14 rupees a litre from 11.50, and on jet fuel exports too. The Chief Economic Adviser says India may need to manage a strong rupee, not a weak one, next financial year, with several agencies expecting Brent below 80 dollars.

Budget season is warming up. The Finance Minister held her seventh pre-Budget meeting. Non-bank lenders want a fund for small business lending run by SIDBI, industry wants new production incentives for batteries and robotics, and the government is examining how it taxes foreign investors' share gains. And the Prime Minister challenged India Inc to raise wages and create jobs after the tax cuts and trade deals.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Now around the world, where one listing dominated the day. Anthropic sold 980 million shares at 83 dollars each, raising about 81 billion dollars, the largest public offering ever, plus another 26 billion in a private placement. The shares opened at 111.50 dollars, 34 percent above the offer price, and briefly valued the company at close to 2 trillion dollars. They then gave back much of that, ending the day up around 17 percent at about 97 dollars.

The debut did not lift the wider mood. The Dow fell about 1,100 points, or 2.2 percent, closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq each lost about 2 percent, and Wall Street's fear gauge is at its highest since March. Nvidia is down about 32 percent since late October.

Asia is taking the hit this morning. Korea's Kospi fell about 4.7 percent and Japan's Nikkei as much as 4.8 percent. Hong Kong's Hang Seng is nearing bear-market territory. The Chinese yuan is at its weakest in more than a month, and Latin American currencies are sliding on the prospect of more American rate hikes.

Oil is a little firmer after Houthi attacks on Riyadh, with Brent near 92 dollars a barrel. But it is still set for a third straight weekly fall. Gold and silver remain close to fourteen-month lows.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money, and the big news is from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. Its board has approved a systematic withdrawal plan, so retirees can draw their provident fund in monthly, quarterly or half-yearly instalments instead of one lump sum, while the rest keeps earning interest. It also cut the minimum balance for final withdrawals from 25 percent to 10 percent, and the waiting period from twelve months to two. And it will let up to 3 percent of inflows go into alternative investment funds.

Two less happy notes from the same body. It says it has no legal way to recover 1,816 crore rupees owed by Reliance Capital. And granting higher pensions to 4.45 lakh applicants could cost about 1.1 lakh crore rupees.

On UPI, a relief for traders. Under a revised plan from the payments corporation, payments between wholesalers and retailers may carry a flat 5 rupee fee, instead of charges of up to 300 rupees proposed earlier.

A tax ruling worth knowing. The Pune bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal deleted a 2.5 lakh rupee addition against a government employee, after accepting that the builder had returned the cash paid for a plot.

Yes Bank's additional tier one bondholders have asked the Reserve Bank to protect investors, after the Supreme Court restored their bonds. The bank and the Reserve Bank are seeking a review.

That's the brief. Today, watch whether the Nifty holds the 25,400 to 25,200 zone after the expected gap-down, whether foreign investors keep buying through the global storm, and how Asia and oil behave through the day. Have a good Friday.
